text:
alex: Quick favor — can someone run a small overhead sanity sweep comparing streaming vs non-streaming for funcalls + structured outputs? Trying to rule out regressions after the kernel changes.

I want: 1) cold-start baseline, 2) steady-state streaming, 3) synchronous funcall path. Keep prompt small (≈32 tokens) and structured JSON output. No need for huge throughput, just latency numbers and 95/99 pctl.

jin: I can run it. Which model/quantization do you want? and should I use toolcall chaining (tool -> tool) or just one function call?

alex: Start with the usual rwd/turbo-8k q4_0 (the perf profile we use on dedicated). Single funcall first, then a 2-step toolchain. Streaming = chunked token events with function result streamed too.

pat: Quick note: the streaming path currently does extra serialization on the control plane if the structured schema is present — might add ~0.6–1.5ms per chunk. Good to confirm.

sam: I have a tiny harness:
```bash
python benchmarks/run_rt_overhead.py \--model rwd/turbo-8k-q4_0 \--prompt-file tests/short_struct_prompt.jsonl \--mode {streaming,sync} \--funcalls 1,2 \--samples 150 
```
It emits per-request latencies and token event timings. Use --samples 150 for decent pctl numbers.

derek: tagging infra: @ci-bot please spin a test dedicated slot (1xA10G) for ~30m so these runs don't hit shared pools.

ci-bot: confirmed — reserved dedicated-1 (A10G) from 1771112250 to 1771114050. Logs will be uploaded to s3://redwood-ci/benchmarks/1771112222/

jin: running now. sending results when done.

[~15m later]

jin: initial numbers attached (raw CSV in S3). Highlights:
- cold-start median: 142ms (streaming) vs 130ms (sync)
- steady-state median per-request (after warm): 26ms (streaming) vs 21ms (sync)
- 95th: 54ms (streaming) vs 39ms (sync)
- funcall chaining (2-step) adds ~12–18ms median extra for both modes

pat: those deltas look like the serialization overhead I mentioned. Do you have token event counts? streaming chunk size seems defaulting to 16 tokens which matches the bump.

jin: yes chunks ~16 tokens, ~3 chunk events for a 48-token completion. CSV has token_event_count.

sam: can you re-run with chunk_size=8 and chunk_size=32 to see sensitivity? I suspect chunk_size decrease will increase per-request CPU overhead but lower tail latencies.

jin: started two runs (8/32). Will report.

[~10m later]

jin: results: chunk_size=8 -> steady median 29ms, 95th 47ms. chunk_size=32 -> median 24ms, 95th 62ms. So smaller chunks slightly higher medians, better tails up to a point; larger chunks reduce median but increase 95th due to batching variability.

alex: great, thanks. Action items:
- pat: can you follow up on the extra control-plane serialization and see if we can short-circuit it when schema is small?
- eng-runtime: add a small perf test to CI that runs this harness with 32 samples to catch regressions (low-cost).
- jin/sam: drop the raw CSVs into the bench folder and add a short summary (1-paragraph) to the S3 link.

pat: will take ownership of the serialization check.

jin: uploading CSVs and writing a one-paragraph summary now. s3://redwood-ci/benchmarks/1771112222/summary.txt

sam: I can draft a tiny CI job. Ping me when CSV URL is final. :thumbsup:

alex: thanks all. if anything obvious pops up in the serialization check, flag it in #eng-runtime and we can decide rollback vs patch.

pat: noted. will report by EOD.

ci-bot: artifact upload complete: s3://redwood-ci/benchmarks/1771112222/{raw.csv,summary.txt,run-config.json}

alex: perfect — closing the loop.
